title: Optimists of Lemmy, what gives you hope about the future?

excerpts.text: All of this will pass. You won't necessarily be able to control any of the variables outside of your own life, but living a virtuous life isn't about becoming the leader of a country or amassing gigantic wealth. It's about doing the right thing, for yourself a

Generally speaking, the world just keeps getting better in ways that matter. Despite all the wars going on, this is probably the most peaceful time in human history; we just see every single conflict thanks to modern telecommunication. There has always been te

All of this push for global fascism and tightening of chains across the world is actually an extinction burst that's happening precisely because the world is waking up. The oligarchs see one last chance to hold onto power before the common people flip the boar
Organising stuff! I'm pulling together a couple friends to a bar and holding a privacy workshop For anyone who feels like practicing privacy is boring and wants do it over a drink.

There's one thing that's happened this year that inspired actual hope in me. (I am generally a cynic, having read too many history books.) [I made a video about Flock buying out their employees](https://youtu.be/umKaBnmSiCE) and, in researching it, learned tha

We're getting to see how bad things get before people change their minds. And people are, it's slow and there are holdouts as well as people that just do not want good things for anyone besides themselves/their tribe. I think the global right is pulling all th
I know that there are good people everywhere who will keep trying. It will take some time, but the pendulum will swing back the other way. People will always keep trying.

There's a quote from HBO's Chernobyl series: > To be a scientist is to be naive. We are so focused on our search for the truth we fail to consider how few actually want us to find it. But it is always there whether we see it or not, whether we choose to or not
